title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction: Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes Grothendieck is axiomatizing tame topology ('modérations'). For a tame structure, the 'ateliers' are lattices of figures Fig(L), carrying the operations and relations ∪, · (intersection), ≤, a 'well-inside' relation ≪ / ≪̊ (roughly: contained in the interior), and an incidence relation |∘|. He is asking what a morphism between such ateliers should be. On the previous page he notes that inverse images f^*: Fig(Y) → Fig(X) behave badly when f is not surjective. f^* then factors through restriction to the image f(X), so some figures go to ∅. Relations of type ≤ / ≪ between 'multiplicités' (the objects being compared) are then not preserved, although ≪̊ and |∘| are. This page diagnoses the trouble. The delicate point is the 'passage au quotient', which takes us outside the notion of a structure-preserving map that is an isomorphism onto its image. In the examples so far (f^* with f surjective, a restriction/embedding map), each 'multiplicité' was carried isomorphically ('en iso'). For general f^* it was carried either isomorphically or to ∅. He then announces cases resembling 'embeddings', where an object is not carried isomorphically. Example 2: let L, L' be spaces of the tame structure, F' ∈ Fig(L'), F' ≠ ∅. Consider Fig(L) → Fig(L×L'), F ↦ F×F' = pr1^*(F)·pr2^*(F'). This is the composite of two maps. The first is pr1^*, an injective lattice map because pr1 is surjective when L' ≠ ∅. The second is Φ ↦ Φ·F with F = pr2^*(F'), i.e. intersection with a fixed figure. The composite is injective and preserves ∪, ·, ≤ (for F' ≠ ∅). It does not preserve the absolute well-inside relation: X ≪ Y in L does not give X×F' ≪ Y×F' in L×L' unless F' is open. The next page makes this precise: ≪̊ must be replaced by a relative version ≪̊_rel (well-inside relative to the ambient figure), and the product notion × by ×_rel. Example 3 (next page, restriction to a sub-modération) is of the same kind. The aim is to delimit which maps between lattices of figures are the 'morphisms' of tame-topological ateliers.
errors: No mathematical error. Composing pr1^* with intersection by pr2^*(F') is correct; injectivity needs F' ≠ ∅, which he states (he writes the hypothesis twice, L'≠∅ and F'≠∅).
The exact meaning of 'multiplicité' and 'iso' on this page is ambiguous. The reading 'each object is sent isomorphically, or to ∅' is a reconstruction, not certain.

ideas.what: Inverse image of figures f^* as a lattice homomorphism. It is injective iff f is surjective; in general it factors through restriction to the image, a quotient.
ideas.modern_name: Stone-type duality between maps of spaces and homomorphisms of Boolean algebras / lattices of definable sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stone (1936); standard in o-minimality (van den Dries 1998)

ideas.what: Product with a fixed nonempty figure, F ↦ F×F', as the composite pr1^* followed by intersection with pr2^*(F'). It preserves ≤ but turns 'interior/well-inside' into a relative notion.
ideas.modern_name: Relative interior / relative topology on a definable subset; morphisms of proximity or contact lattices
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; well-inside relations in de Vries (1962), proximity lattices (Jung–Sünderhauf 1996)

ideas.what: The programme of defining morphisms between 'ateliers' of a tame topology: lattices of figures with relations ≤, ≪̊, |∘|.
ideas.modern_name: Point-free / lattice-theoretic axiomatization of tame (o-minimal-like) topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Programme announced in Esquisse d'un programme §5 (topologie modérée); realized differently by o-minimality (van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6, only as a general programme; the atelier formalism is not published

missed.claim: Grothendieck tries to axiomatize tame topology point-free. He works with lattices of figures carrying a 'well-inside' relation and an incidence relation, and seeks the correct morphisms. He notes that inverse images along non-surjective maps and products with a fixed figure force relative versions of ≪̊ and ×. This lattice-theoretic approach to o-minimal / tame geometry was never developed in the literature, which followed the model-theoretic route instead.
missed.quote: Le point délicat ici, est apparemment dans la notion de passage au quotient ... qui nous fait sortir de la notion de l'homéomorphisme
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: There is a possible bridge to de Vries / contact-algebra duality and proximity lattices from point-free topology. Applied to Boolean algebras of definable sets with a well-inside relation, it could give a duality-theoretic account of o-minimal structures and their morphisms.

missed.claim: The relations ≤, ≪̊ and the need for a relative ≪̊_rel under intersection with a non-open figure match the axiomatics of proximity/contact lattices. That literature (de Vries, Jung–Sünderhauf, Bezhanishvili et al.) was never connected to Grothendieck's tame topology.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This suggests treating tame structures as proximity lattices closed under products and inverse images. That might clarify which lattice maps correspond to definable maps.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is elementary: injectivity of pr1^*, and intersection with a fixed figure breaking the absolute interior relation. Interest lies only in the unpublished attempt at a point-free 'atelier' formalism for tame topology, of which this page is a small exploratory step.
transcription_corrections: 'au "théorème" d'un ordinateur' is almost certainly wrong. The image suggests something like 'au "plongement" d'un [atelier?] dans un autre, où, au contraire, une multiplicité n'est pas transformée en iso'.
'ou de i_K' may be 'ou de i_*' (direct image along an inclusion), consistent with the previous page's 'f^*, i_*'.
'L, L' deux ensembles' is uncertain; it may read 'deux espaces' or 'deux ens.'. The hypothesis 'F' ≠ ∅' is inserted above the line as a correction.
'd'une multiplication ordinaire dans Fig(L×L')' is doubtful. The image reads more like 'et d'une application [?], savoir la ... à Fig(L×L'): Φ ↦ Φ·F (où F = pr_2^*(F'))'.
The last line likely reads roughly 'application qui (si F' est non vide) a [toutes?] les propriétés formelles ... [de] multiplicité[s] [?]'. It is partially illegible.
